title: Graceful debounce and persistent spinner for icon toggle sets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Icon-only toggles and small action buttons exhibit visual jitter and layout shift when a spinner briefly appears on click. In high-frequency flows (quick toggles), the spinner flash creates perceived slowness and accessibility confusion. We also have inconsistent token fallbacks between light/dark and the new high-contrast theme leading to color regressions.

Goal: Introduce a small debounce window and a persistent spinner affordance for icon toggle sets that: (1) prevents micro-flash for operations under the debounce threshold, (2) presents a stable spinner position/size for longer operations, (3) respects theme token fallbacks and WCAG contrast targets, (4) provides a cancelable visual state for interrupted interactions, and (5) is backward-compatible with existing button API/props.

Scope: Design tokens, button component visual states, motion timing, a11y labels for spinner states, icon layout constraints, and documentation updates. Implementation to be paired with engineering patch in ui-lib runtime release ui-lib-2.14.

Acceptance criteria:
- Short actions (<120ms) show no spinner or layout shift; the control briefly shows an optimistic pressed state then returns.
- Actions between 120ms and 600ms show a subtle placeholder (low-cost shimmer) rather than the full spinner.
- Actions >600ms show a full spinner sized and anchored to the icon center; spinner size uses token --spinner-size-sm and does not change the component bounding box.
- Token fallbacks: when a theme token is missing, the component uses theme-anchor tokens (token list in attachments) and passes color contrast >= 3:1 for idle labels and >= 4.5:1 for critical disabled states where text is present.
- Spinner exposes aria-live updates ("Loading" / "Complete") and a visually-hidden cancel hint if the action is cancelable.
- No layout shift regression in RTL or compact density.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Debounce thresholds chosen after measuring median API latencies in product flows; we opted for slightly larger thresholds to reduce perceived flicker at the cost of marginally delaying spinner feedback.
- Persistent spinner is centered over the icon and layered with prefer-reduced-motion support: when reduced-motion is enabled, spinner cross-fades instead of rotating.
- We avoid increasing hit-target size in this change to limit surface-area regressions; follow-up ticket will address hit target parity for mini-action controls.

Rollout plan:
1) Ship design tokens and visual spec to engineering (ui-lib-2.14).
2) Feature-flag runtime behavior behind "button-spinner-debounce" for canary in staging.
3) Run regression harness on core flows (chat composer, message actions, nav icon sets).
4) Gradual rollout, monitor console telemetry for button click latencies and spinner incidence.

Notes for engineering:
- Token names referenced in attachments. Keep backward-compatible aliases for --spinner-size-sm and --icon-press-offset.
- Provide boolean prop spinnerCancelable and aria attributes per spec.
- Provide a static CSS class to opt-out for integrators who need legacy behavior.
comments: 2025-03-11 - Initial design exploration completed. Ran A/B test sketches comparing 100ms vs 150ms debounce. Team prefers 120ms median; reduces flicker while keeping responsiveness.

2025-03-12 - UX review with PM (Juno Martinez) and Eng lead (Samir Gupta). Agreed to require aria-live updates and to support reduced-motion. Engineering asked for explicit token fallbacks and small static class for legacy opt-out.
2025-03-13 - Figma prototypes uploaded (see attachments). Early developer feedback: spinner stacking caused z-index conflicts in popover groups; added z-index guidance to spec.
2025-03-14 - Accessibility review: a11y engineer (Nina Zhou) verified announce strings and suggested using role=progressbar for longer-running operations; added acceptability criteria for aria roles.

2025-03-17 - Design QA pass: validated compact and comfortable densities, RTL, and high-contrast theme. Found one regression where disabled icon color fell below contrast target in high-contrast theme; updated token mapping and blocked engineering until fix applied.
2025-03-18 - Engineering PR opened: github.com/redwood/ui-lib/pull/4822. Assigned to Liam for design review on visual deltas. Added canary flag in staging config.
